To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) CEP-AOP is the first protocol to provide message franking with minimum leakage, whereby only the abusive parts of the message are revealed to the third party; 2) CEP-AOPS2 is the first protocol that provides message franking with privacy for all the non-abusive blocks, and 3) CEP2 is the first multi-opening secure CEM construction using a single PRF evaluation over a message, and only relying on standard security assumptions of the underlying primitives
we have formalized a new privacy notion for message franking protocols called MO-IND-PO.
we provide the first formal treatment for message franking protocols, where the privacy of a message can be preserved, while only the abusive blocks of the message are leaked.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: - We provide a new privacy notion for multi-opening indistinquishability with after opening privacy, which forces an adversary in a chosen ciphertext attack to distinguish encrypted abusive blocks.
the formal treatment of message privacy in franking protocols.
the design of message franking schemes with privacy, which is a crucial requirement in order to be deployed in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we provide the first formal treatment for message franking protocols, with minimum leakage whereby the receiver can open only the abusive blocks of a message, while the rest remain private, thus achieving After Opening Privacy.
we provide the first message franking protocol which is multi-opening, after opening privacy, and computationally efficient.
we provide the first multi-opening secure and privacy preserving message franking protocols, with minimum leakage and communication cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we initiate and formalize a new privacy notion in the context of message franking with after opening privacy.

the CEP-AOP protocols are the first message franking protocols which provide the receiver the ability of after opening privacy, thus achieving the minimum leakage of only abusive message blocks, which is the ultimate goal of message franking.

we provide a new privacy definition for multi-opening message franking protocols, which is the first to consider after opening privacy, and we design and analyze two constructions which adhere to the definition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the receiver does not need to reveal the opening key and the entire message to the third-party.
we provide the first message franking protocols which are private after the opening of abusive blocks, thus achieving the best of both worlds, i.e., privacy and accountability.
the new privacy definition we provide, is more meaningful and realistic in practice, since it allows to keep the confidentiality of the non-abusive blocks.
